bug_semantics: Kraken agents transfer container-image blobs peer-to-peer as torrent pieces. Piece integrity inside the agent's content-addressable store is validated exclusively against per-piece CRC32 sums: agentstorage Torrent.writePiece() computes core.PieceHash() (crc32.NewIEEE()) over downloaded bytes and accepts the piece when h.Sum32() == metaInfo.GetPieceSum(pi); metainfo.calcPieceSums() builds those expected sums with the same CRC32. CRC32 (IEEE) is not a cryptographic integrity check and is trivially forgeable, so a malicious peer or on-path attacker can substitute blob content whose per-piece CRC32 still matches and poison the agent's cache; the poisoned blob is subsequently served to other peers, enabling container-image content forgery and downstream RCE (CWE-354).
flaw_origin: Commit 5296d690e069c78d2df5bedec24611a9bb298ca9 ("Change piece hash to crc32 and metainfo column to MEDIUMBLOB", 2017-11-21, author Cody Gibb) first replaced the previous SHA-1 piece hashing with CRC32 in torlib: it deletes the sha1-based Info.PieceHash() from torlib/info.go and adds torlib/piece_hash.go defining PieceHash() = crc32.NewIEEE(), the exact mechanism later relocated verbatim into core/piece_hash.go by the 2018 consolidation move cd2fcfc5e56d16fef369093cc3020e1dba3d2d92 (a package move, not an origin). The direct parent 9c2ea795e6e58680375e4132c31acc8ec54b6e65 still computes piece hashes with crypto/sha1, so the forgeable-checksum mechanism is absent there.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names author and committer Cody Gibb <codyg@uber.com>; its message is a plain Phabricator change ("Change piece hash to crc32 and metainfo column to MEDIUMBLOB", Summary about mysql TEXT column overflow when benchmarking large files), with no Co-Authored-By, no Generated-with, and no bot identity. 2017 predates AI codegen tools; no AI marker exists on the object.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xpm6-xhxf-22h5 / CVE-2026-75625 describes agents failing to verify blob integrity against the expected SHA-256 digest, relying on forgeable CRC32 piece sums, enabling cache poisoning and RCE (CWE-354, CVSS 9.0); disclosure 2026-08.

Vulnerable mechanism at HEAD: core/piece_hash.go returns crc32.NewIEEE() / crc32.ChecksumIEEE; lib/torrent/storage/agentstorage/torrent.go writePiece() (lines ~180-199) accepts a downloaded piece when its CRC32 equals metaInfo.GetPieceSum(pi); core/metainfo.go calcPieceSums() (~line 145) derives expected sums with PieceHash(). No SHA-256 verification gates the P2P piece path in the clone's history (git grep for sha256 in agent/agentclient, agent/agentserver, lib/torrent piece paths finds none).

BIC diff: `git show 5296d690e069c78d2df5bedec24611a9bb298ca9` deletes `-h := sha1.New()` / Info.PieceHash() in torlib/info.go and adds `+"hash/crc32"` / `+func PieceHash() hash.Hash32 { return crc32.NewIEEE() }` in new file torlib/piece_hash.go; commit message explicitly states "Change hashing algorithm from sha1 to crc32" and acknowledges "crc32 is not cryptographically secure".

Parent verification: parent 9c2ea795e6e58680375e4132c31acc8ec54b6e65 tree contains torlib/info.go with crypto/sha1 piece hashing and no torlib/piece_hash.go (git grep over the parent tree shows sha1-based PieceHash; the crc32 file does not exist), so the forgeable-checksum lines are absent from the immediate parent.

Move disambiguation: the 2018 commit cd2fcfc5e56d16fef369093cc3020e1dba3d2d92 ("Consolidate Kraken types in new core package") merely relocates torlib/piece_hash.go to core/piece_hash.go — a package move, excluded from BIC by protocol.

Tag membership: both the sha1 state and the BIC are ancestors of the repo's earliest tag v0.1.0 (merge-base checks), so the vulnerable CRC32 mechanism ships in every tagged release; no later tag changes PieceHash().

Unpatched: as of HEAD (2026-08-25 main, commit b123998b3dbcfe90555463f6ae8bbe129a027b2c), core/piece_hash.go still returns CRC32 and no commit in core/piece_hash.go, torlib/piece_hash.go history replaces it with a cryptographic hash (git log -S 'sha256' over both paths is empty); the advisory lists no fixed version.
reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory's mechanism is agent-side piece validation keyed on forgeable CRC32 sums rather than a cryptographic digest, allowing P2P cache poisoning. BIC choice: the smallest commit that first wrote the CRC32 piece-hash mechanism is 5296d690e069c78d2df5bedec24611a9bb298ca9, which swapped SHA-1 for CRC32 in torlib; the 2018 core-package consolidation is a move and the agentstorage writePiece call sites are consumers of that mechanism, not origins. Parent verification: the immediate parent's tree uses crypto/sha1 for piece hashes and lacks the CRC32 implementation, satisfying introducer_parent_absent=true by direct tree inspection. Tag/version cross-check: the BIC predates the earliest tag v0.1.0, and the mechanism persists through HEAD, covering the advisory's affected range. AI decision: the BIC commit object shows a single human author/committer (Cody Gibb) with a plain engineering message and no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot trailer; under BIC-only attribution the verdict is NOT_AI. The advisory notes a SHA-256 verification gap in agent blob handling; that gap is an instance of the same absent-cryptographic-integrity mechanism introduced here, not a separate write path.
remaining_gap: Unpatched as of the audited HEAD (2026-08-25): no public commit replaces CRC32 piece verification or adds SHA-256 gating to the P2P piece path, and the advisory lists no patched version, so fix_sha/direct_fix_sha are null under the unpatched rule. The advisory's precise affected-version range is not published (GitHub advisory lists ranges as unknown in the bundle), but the mechanism's presence from v0.1.0 through HEAD makes the closed NOT_AI result unaffected.

unpatched.reason: No public commit replaces CRC32 piece verification or adds SHA-256 gating to the P2P piece path as of audited HEAD (2026-08-25); the advisory lists no patched version.

potential_fix.approach: Upgrade piece verification from CRC32 to SHA-256 (or BLAKE3) with the expected digest carried in signed metadata, and reject pieces whose digest check fails.
potential_fix.rationale: A cryptographic per-piece digest makes forged-piece injection computationally infeasible, closing the torrent-piece corruption path.
